content.title: About
content.content: Garlic bread with melted cheese is a popular snack item in fast‑food chains and restaurants. A loaf, usually a baguette or ciabatta, is brushed with a mixture of butter, minced garlic and herbs, then topped with shredded cheese (commonly mozzarella or cheddar) and baked until golden and bubbly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a variation of traditional Italian focaccia.
Garlic’s allicin compounds interact with the fatty acids in cheese, enhancing aroma and flavor.
Garlic cheese bread is often served alongside pizza, pasta and salads, and is also enjoyed as a standalone snack.
Some restaurants add spices such as paprika or oregano to the cheese blend for extra zest.
Vegan versions replace dairy cheese with plant‑based alternatives while keeping the garlic‑butter base.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Garlic contains sulfur compounds like allicin that have antioxidant properties and support immune function.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese, especially hard varieties, provides calcium essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Cheese adds animal protein that aids tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Moderate cheese consumption can raise HDL (good) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Dietary fiber from bread
items.content: When whole‑grain bread is used, it contributes dietary fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or lactose may react to the cheese component.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty, making the dish high in sodium, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Garlic bread with cheese is calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Gastro‑esophageal reflux
items.content: The fat in cheese can exacerbate heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, straight from the oven. Cut into bite‑size pieces, pair with salads or soups, or use as a base for sandwiches. For a lighter version, choose whole‑grain bread and low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave before serving. Freezing is not recommended as the cheese may become grainy.
